title: Unit 3 : Session 9 : SLO 1 — Restoring Division Algorithm (Procedure)
sections: A. Sign Bit → 4. Indicates positive or negative
B. Negative Remainder → 5. Triggered when subtraction fails
C. Quotient Register → 3. Stores result bits (0 or 1)
D. Shift Step → 2. Logical left shift on registers
E. Restoring Step → 1. Add divisor to restore remainder
Section B: Fill in the Blanks (Understand)
The restoring division algorithm is primarily used for BINARY division of binary numbers.
If subtraction in a cycle produces a NEGATIVE remainder, the algorithm restores the previous value.
The REMAINDER register is shifted left with the quotient during each iteration.
The divisor is SUBTRACTED from the remainder in each cycle.
The quotient bit is set to 1 if the subtraction is successful.
